sections.h2: What kind of city is West Palm Beach, and why does that shape a tax bill?
sections.html:
West Palm Beach is the county seat of Palm Beach County, so the same city that holds the courthouse also sits inside the county's tax machinery. The city's own history page says it was incorporated on November 5, 1894, two years ahead of Miami, and counted about 1,000 residents in 1895. It now estimates more than 120,000 people.

The housing stock varies a great deal from one end of town to the other. The city's history page names the shopping and dining districts of The Square, Clematis Street, Antique Row and Northwood Village, and it points to Grassy Waters Everglades Preserve on the western edge. A bungalow near Northwood and a newer place out west do not share a value history, which is why the parcel record matters more than any citywide average.

Other landmarks the city lists include the Kravis Center for the Performing Arts and the Norton Museum of Art. Florida's first junior college, Palm Beach Jr. College, opened here in 1933, and the airport moved thousands of servicemen during World War II.

sections.h2: Which offices touch a West Palm Beach property tax bill?
sections.html:
Two county offices do the work, and the city only adds its own levy. The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser sets values and handles exemptions, while the Palm Beach County Tax Collector mails and collects the bill.

The collector says it sends more than 600,000 bills each year, with the mailing wrapping up by November 1. Money collected is split among county and city governments, the school district, fire departments, libraries, parks, children's services and the healthcare district.

A bill follows the mailing address on file at the appraiser. After a sale or a move, update that record, or send the collector's Property Sold Form so the notice reaches the new owner instead of piling up at an old address.

sections.h2: What millage rates sit on a West Palm Beach parcel?
sections.html:
A parcel inside the city carries several layers of millage, and the appraiser's rate page shows each layer in one list. A mill is one dollar of tax for every thousand dollars of taxable value.

The same page shows a downtown development authority levy of 0.9700 for 2025 and 2.0000 proposed for 2026. It reaches only parcels inside that district. Rather than adding columns yourself, look up the parcel and read its own total.

sections.h2: How does the payment calendar work in Palm Beach County?
sections.html:
Bills can be paid from November 1 through March 31, and the collector's discount shrinks month by month: 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. March carries no discount.

  • Delinquent bills cannot be paid online, so allow time for an office or mail payment.
  • To count for a month, a payment must arrive by that month's last working day. A postmark does not prove timely payment.
  • A due date that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

The collector also keeps an important dates page. Check it before setting a closing near the end of a discount month, since an extra percentage point on a large bill is real money.

sections.h2: What follows April 1 for an unpaid Palm Beach County bill?
sections.html:
Penalties and interest attach, and the collector later auctions a tax certificate. Under s. 197.402 the sale takes place 60 days after the delinquency date or on June 1, whichever comes later.

A certificate is a first lien that an investor buys by paying the tax. When no investor bids, the certificate is struck to the county and accrues 18 percent a year, or 1.5 percent a month. Redeeming one means paying the tax, the interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee.

After two years of nonpayment the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed under s. 197.502. The Clerk and Comptroller runs that sale, and the owner may redeem until the sale occurs. The auction's high bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is more, and pays in full within 24 hours under s. 197.542.

sections.h2: How can a West Palm Beach owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Start with a call to the appraiser, then file with the Value Adjustment Board if the matter stays open. The appraiser's office offers an informal conference at 561.355.3230 and says that talking to staff does not extend the filing deadline.

The board has five members: two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizens. It relies on special magistrates, who hear cases on valuation, portability denials, deferrals and change of ownership findings and recommend decisions, while the board makes the final ruling. The Clerk and Comptroller administers the process separately from the appraiser.

  • The petition is due within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. The 2026 deadline was September 14, and it has passed.
  • The board may charge up to $20 to file.
  • Single parcels can be filed online through the clerk's portal. Contiguous parcels go by mail or in person.
  • Mail goes to PO Box 4036, West Palm Beach, FL 33402. In person or by courier, the office is at 301 North Olive Avenue, Room 206.
  • An incomplete petition gets a Clerk's Notice with 10 calendar days to fix it.

sections.h2: What should a seller in West Palm Beach settle before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the collector for a payoff figure that runs through the closing date, and check whether a certificate exists on the parcel. The collector posts a delinquent list online, and county-held certificates can be searched through its RealAuction link.

  • Homestead ends with the sale, and the next January 1 resets the assessment to just value, so the buyer's bill can differ sharply from yours.
  • A seller buying again in Florida can look into portability, which has its own three-year window and a Form DR-501T.
  • Deed stamps run 70 cents per $100 of price here, because the county is not Miami-Dade, and the contract says which side pays.
  • Clerk recording charges follow s. 28.24, and the title agent adds both to the settlement statement.

The collector's home page also points owners to a statewide property tax amendment. Ask which changes reach your parcel before you plan around them.

sections.h2: What does the sample Palm Beach County bill actually show?
sections.html:
The collector posts a sample bill with numbered callouts. It identifies the property control number, owners, situs address, exemptions, and the assessed, exempt and taxable values, then lists the amount due in each discount month. A QR code leads to the payment portal.

Taxable value is assessed value minus exemptions. Each authority's millage is multiplied against it to produce the ad valorem total, and non-ad valorem assessments such as solid waste fees are added on top. When a payoff statement looks high, compare its lines with this layout.

The TRIM notice arrives in August with proposed values and hearing dates, local taxing bodies hold September hearings, and the collector mails bills in November.

faqs.q: What is the West Palm Beach city millage rate on the appraiser's list?
faqs.a: The appraiser's rate page shows 8.1308 mills for the city in 2025 and a proposed 8.1308 for 2026, with a separate city debt service line. Confirm the certified figure with the tax collector.

faqs.q: When does a West Palm Beach tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Taxes paid in full by March 31 avoid penalties, and after April 1 the bill can no longer be paid online.

faqs.q: Which discount applies if I pay in December?
faqs.a: The collector's schedule gives 3 percent in December. November is 4 percent, January is 2, February is 1, and March has none.

faqs.q: What does redeeming a Palm Beach County certificate cost?
faqs.a: You pay the delinquent tax, accrued interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee, per the collector's tax certificate page.

faqs.q: Who holds the tax deed sale in Palm Beach County?
faqs.a: The Clerk and Comptroller conducts it. Bidders post a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater, and must pay in full within 24 hours.
